_note: Joel Smyth's stated 1-N WR ranking for 2026 (his 'top 48'). Ranked board, not note-only — he narrates a consistent numbered order (explicit numbers like 'at number one', 'right after that at 19', '21 I have', 'at 23', 'GJ Moore at 24', '29 though') with clear sequential narration between anchors. posRank covers his confident, unambiguous top 34 only. Beyond that a few captioned names were too garbled or re-shuffled mid-narration to trust an exact ordinal (a Miami WR captioned 'L Maki' at his stated #23 could not be identified and was dropped entirely, per the injection rule against guessing garbled names) — those later mentions (Godwin, Metcalf, Wilson, Sutton, Debo, Addison, Johnston, Meyers, Pittman, Reed, Doubs) are captured note-only with no posRank so they add reasoning without casting a vote past the point his numbering got unreliable. Two garbled names WERE resolved from strong surrounding context and kept: 'Am I Boa'/'Greg Bua' = Emeka Egbuka (Tampa Bay/Baker Mayfield/Mike Evans/Liam Cohen-to-HC context is unambiguous), and 'a Dunay'/'GJ Moore' = Rome Odunze / DJ Moore (Bears trio and Bills/Diggs context respectively).
_confidence: Captured from YouTube auto-captions via /watch transcript detail, no frames. Rank 23 (garbled name, Miami WR under McDaniel) dropped, could not confidently resolve. Odunze/Loveland's exact 25/26 ordering is inferred from narrative sequence rather than an explicit stated number, since he re-visits the Bears trio as a group after already giving Burden its own #21 — treat as approximate within that pair. Evans' rank is fuzzy by his own admission ('switched that 28 to like 32, could move around a lot') due to breaking thigh injury news — captured as note-only rather than a fixed slot for that reason.
ranksAre: positional (WR only) for top 34; note-only beyond that

ja'marr chase.note: Clear #1. Stability: 5 years in NFL, 5x fantasy WR1 seasons, versatile enough defenses can't take him away, elite QB play even with Flacco filling in for an injured Burrow.

puka nacua.note: Clear #2 despite flaws last year (43rd in routes/game, only 4 end-zone targets). Led the NFL in targets-per-route (36-38%) by a wide margin — per-route he's in a league of his own. Could be even better if the Rams offense as a whole regresses a bit.

amon-ra st. brown.note: Very close with JSN, edges him on stability — top-5 receiver 3 straight years. Basically equal to JSN's huge 2025 season once you remove St. Brown's concussion game. Not worried about Petting's arrival; Detroit funnels volume to its #1 WR and TE.

jaxon smith-njigba.note: 2025 was close to perfect (36% target share, highest since 2012; 73% catch rate on downfield targets, top-3 since 2015) but Kubiak is gone and his past two OC departures both saw explosive-play offenses decline. More target competition too (Shaheed, Tory Horton). End of the first tier — good, not Chase-level, but ahead of CD Lamb.

ceedee lamb.note: Extremely consistent, mostly a low-end WR1 outside his one monster season. Ran into real bad luck last year (touchdown regression despite heavy target/red-zone volume). Trading some upside for floor — you're betting on the floor over the ceiling here.

justin jefferson.note: Caution flag: unnecessary risk this high given so many good RBs are available in this range instead. Lots of target competition (Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings) and a QB fit (Kyler Murray) that doesn't love deep/downfield throwers as much.

drake london.note: Every Michael Penix passing TD in 2 NFL seasons has gone to London. 33% target share, elite yards/route with Penix. Floor is lower without him healthy but ceiling remains great; Darnell Mooney's departure hasn't mattered (3 games without him, never under 15 targets).

a.j. brown.note: Same shape as London — low floor, huge ceiling, for different reasons. Patriots + Drake May's deep-ball accuracy is a great fit; only Diggs and Bourne were better than May on deep-ball production last year. Real injury risk (2 hamstring injuries + knee wear), but second-half-healthy version was top-5 numbers.

george pickens.note: Overall-WR1-upside handcuff to Lamb; best fantasy WR the month Lamb was out, still WR8 even with Lamb back despite a 22% target share. Target share should climb as Dak/Pickens chemistry (slow start last year) is already established now.

rashee rice.note: Better fantasy player than NFL player — heavy scheme/system usage (screens, goal-line work, second only to Adams in red-zone work) masks NFL flaws. Concern: Matt Nagy (who fed Rice specifically) is gone, though Andy Reid remains. Still top-10 range for fantasy purposes even if not a true top-12 NFL receiver.

nico collins.note: Was WR2 overall in fantasy in his complete 2024 games; injury/concussion history is real and frustrating. Target competition is arguably worse this year (Jaden Higgins no longer a rookie, David Montgomery added) but still a strong floor pick, good for someone punting RB/QB early.

devonta smith.note: Hamstring injury news is annoying (also affects Mai Lemon behind him), but multiple prior stretches show he's the clear #1 when AJ Brown is out (targets/route jump toward 30%). Was miscast in a heavy slot role last year for a QB (Hurts) who wants to chuck it deep outside — new OC Sean Mannion's scheme (more Matt LaFleur-style, more outside usage) should fit him much better.

malik nabers.note: More comfortable with the knee than most; news has been good. Was WR6 as a rookie on the number-one target volume in the NFL, but passing volume should be lower this year and Matt Nagy's offense is a concern. Expect closer to ADP, not the huge outlier some are projecting.

chris olave.note: Injury history (season-ending concussion risk) is still scary, but finishes since his rookie year (WR26, WR19, WR53, then WR7 last year) show real swings. Jordan Tyson's arrival could eat into some of his post-Shaheed-trade volume bump — not a pick he's dying to make at his current ADP (WR12).

tee higgins.note: Main risk is nagging injuries + Burrow's own injury risk; otherwise unchanged elite situation. WR5 in points/game two years ago, WR8 last year with either Burrow or Flacco throwing to him. Being drafted around WR18 — thinks that's too low for his on-field ceiling (a true WR1, not a WR2, when healthy).

jaylen waddle.note: Sean Payton publicly told a reporter to draft Waddle — same thing he said about Michael Thomas before his monster target-volume season. Traded from a run-heavy, low-pass-rate Miami offense (31st in pass rate over expected) to Denver, which led the NFL in pass attempts/game and was 7th in team receiving fantasy points last year with a far worse WR corps. Missed only 7 games in 5 years — durable. Going in the WR20s, doesn't need to be reached for.

zay flowers.note: Was WR12 in the 13 games Lamar Jackson played, not a tiny sample. Rashod Bateman staying at WR2 is good for Flowers' target competition. Mark Andrews' efficiency collapsed last year, opening more room. New OC (Declan Doyle from Chicago) is unproven as a play-caller but uses him in a lot of motion; passing volume upside if Baltimore climbs off dead-last in pass attempts/game.

tetairoa mcmillan.note: Should beat his WR21 rookie finish — a lot of last year's miscues are typical rookie-WR2 mistakes that should shrink. High-value targets already; volume should outpace raw target count.

terry mclaurin.note: Explicitly at 19. Was wrong to like him less last year (correctly, in hindsight) given inevitable TD regression once Deebo Samuel arrived. This year Jayden Daniels presumed healthy, Debo gone (traded for Okonkwo), most red-zone TDs vacated on the team, and a new OC (David Blough... offense) that uses him all over the field instead of pinning him to one side running go/curl routes. Still only 31 despite 8 NFL years (came out of college late).

emeka egbuka.note: NAME RESOLVED FROM CONTEXT (captions read 'Am I Boa'/'Greg Bua'). Incredible start (20.5 PPG through 5 weeks) before a hamstring injury derailed the year. New OC Zac Robinson (from the Rams under Sean McVay) is a real downgrade risk vs. outgoing Liam Cohen, but expected to be the clear #1 target with Mike Evans gone and a hopefully-healthier Baker Mayfield.

luther burden iii.note: Explicitly at 21. Ben Johnson extremely high on him through camp; his 2025 connection with Caleb Williams was far better on a per-route basis than DJ Moore's or Rome Odunze's. Efficiency was great, and Ben Johnson's Chicago offense should throw more in the red zone than his old Detroit offense did.

garrett wilson.note: Doesn't dislike him — it's that basically the entire WR13-21 range is receivers he'd rather draft first. Projects closer to WR15-18. Still hasn't had a true fantasy-WR1 season despite huge talent; Jets added two first-round receiving threats (Adonai Mitchell competing for work) and an unproven-but-likely-upgrade QB in Justin Fields' replacement. Wants to draft with confidence, and this isn't that.

dj moore.note: NAME RESOLVED FROM CONTEXT (captions read 'GJ Moore'). Explicitly at 24. Literal and volume opportunity in Buffalo — Stefon Diggs (the WR1 there for 4 straight years) is gone, offense and QB play are elite. Counterpoint: he was genuinely bad last year, the 4th receiving option on his own Bears team by season's end. Taking the shot on opportunity over 2025 tape.

rome odunze.note: Order relative to Loveland inferred from narrative sequence (discussed first of the Bears trio), not an explicit stated number — treat rank as approximate, roughly mid-20s. Before the injury/through week 8 he was WR10, 11th-best target volume per route run, and 2nd in the NFL (behind Adams) in 'valuable targets' (15+ air yards or red-zone) — doesn't need 10 targets/game to be productive. Chicago runs a lot of 12 personnel (most in the NFL) which concentrates volume on the top-3 pass catchers; Odunze's efficiency in 12 personnel was 2nd-best in the NFL.

colston loveland.note: Third of the Bears trio (Odunze, Burden, Loveland) — no individual posRank given, roughly the same range as Odunze. Extremely good red-zone volume; DJ Moore's departure (who had solid red-zone/end-zone work himself) opens up value there.

davante adams.note: Not the most bullish — expects real TD regression (from 18 to maybe 12, still good) with no clear path to fully offset it. Was WR9 in fantasy last year despite under 800 receiving yards; his yards-over-expected was -106 (versus Nacua's league-best +417) — the volume is more 'valuable' than efficient. Prefers other options in this range for true WR1 upside hunting; injury/age risk (hamstring) is also a factor.

christian watson.note: Efficiency is legitimately elite, but volume has never been consistent (never topped 7 targets/game even during his best fantasy stretch, which also came without Tucker Kraft on the field). Ranked just above Mike Evans in this build.

mike evans.note: Was tracking around 28 but Smyth explicitly moved him down toward ~32 due to fresh thigh/soft-tissue injury news mid-recording ('switched that 28 to like 32, could move around a lot over the next two weeks') — too unstable to assign a fixed posRank here. If healthy, the situation (post-Liam-Cohen-departure, still a talented WR) is good; the risk is losing a mid-round pick to recurring soft-tissue injuries all season.

parker washington.note: Explicitly at 29 despite an ADP around WR38 — a real conviction pick, not a default ranking. In the final month of last season he out-produced Meyers and Brian Thomas Jr. combined in routes/yards/fantasy points; 2nd in the NFL in yards/route over that 8-game stretch (only Nacua was better). Strong camp reports, contested-catch ability despite size, could get paid before the season starts.

jameson williams.note: Concerned about new OC Drew Petting favoring the TE (Sam LaPorta) more, which could compress JMO's already-low target share on a St. Brown/Gibbs-heavy offense. Boom/bust: 8 games in the past 3 years under 10 receiving yards, but also full-season-long-speed upside.

carnell tate.note: His favorite of the Tate/Tyson/Lemon rookie trio. Cam Ward's downfield, contested-catch-friendly style (even if he's not yet a great NFL QB) fits Tate's game well.

jordyn tyson.note: Part of the Tate/Tyson/Lemon rookie trio, ranked just behind Tate. A top-10 pick at the position; looked healthy in camp.

makai lemon.note: Third of the rookie trio, ranked lowest of the three mainly due to recurring hamstring injury concerns.

brian thomas jr..note: 'End of the tier' (his stated 28-32 range) — ranked below Parker Washington partly due to a brutal early-season CB schedule (7 straight weeks of tough matchups) that Washington, working more from the slot, avoids. Still likes the talent and thinks he 'can be back' once the schedule eases.

marvin harrison jr..note: The player he'd most want to be wrong about — still a believer in the talent (especially dynasty-wise) but fantasy-unproven, and buried in target competition (Trey McBride is the clear #1, plus Michael Wilson and pass-catching RB Jeremiyah Love) on a offense that may not throw or score much. His real value is red-zone work — #2 in the NFL in end-zone targets/game since 2024 (behind only Davante Adams).

chris godwin jr..note: Sneaky upside pick. Was WR2 overall two years ago pre-injury; last year's return efficiency wasn't bad given the injury severity. Another full offseason to heal, Mike Evans now out of the way, a real OC upgrade — likes him meaningfully more than his ~WR40 ADP.

dk metcalf.note: A perennial fade for him — hasn't been a top-20 WR in 5+ years. Deep-target role got cut in half moving from Seattle to a Steelers offense that doesn't throw deep and plays almost no scheme designed to beat man coverage, which is specifically what hurt him and Rodgers' connection last year. Doesn't see the fit improving enough (Arthur Smith to Mark McCarthy) to matter at Rodgers' age.

michael wilson.note: Grouped as one of the 'weird' fades/likes in the tail of the board — mentioned mainly as target competition context for Marvin Harrison Jr.

josh downs.note: Likes him, especially in PPR. Real (per him) rumors of more two-TE-set usage and more outside snaps (slot role dropping from ~80% to ~65%, which he considers fine). Good Daniel Jones fit; sneaky red-zone upside (14 red-zone targets last year, top-20 among WRs). Michael Pittman being out helps; rookie-year usage (70% snaps) was a 13 PPG-in-career pace.

courtland sutton.note: A fade — doesn't get the ~WR32 ADP given a career of mostly poor finishes (WR62, WR41, WR39, WR25, then one strong WR15 year) and Sutton himself publicly conceding the WR2/'1A' role to Jaylen Waddle in Denver, which should cut into his red-zone/target volume and make him more man-coverage-dependent and boom/bust.

deebo samuel.note: Interesting, especially if Mike Evans' injury is worse than currently known — was solid last year and San Francisco is a better fit for him than Washington was.

jordan addison.note: Would like him more without Jauan Jennings added to the target competition and with a better stylistic QB fit than Kyler Murray.

quentin johnston.note: Doesn't mind bumping him up a few spots — thinks the offense is spread out but that Tre' Harris is a real receiver, so views Johnston as more of an offensive-upgrade beneficiary than a true WR1 there.

jakobi meyers.note: A fade — good NFL player, but doesn't see much fantasy upside left at this point in his career/role.

michael pittman jr..note: Efficiency was underwhelming even before Daniel Jones' injury affected things. Moving to Pittsburgh as a clear WR2 (less volume than he already lacked in Indy) — likes the raw NFL fit for Rodgers' short-area game but doesn't see much fantasy pass-catching value.

jayden reed.note: Doesn't mind him this year if you want exposure there — Green Bay paid him, and Romeo Doubs' departure (if it happens) helps. Flashes at times.

romeo doubs.note: 'Half green' — loved him before camp, but camp reports haven't been great. If he's the clear WR2 in New England by the start of the season he likes him again; that offense (see AJ Brown) is great for receivers and he doesn't need huge target volume to be a valuable, TD-heavy flyer late in drafts (WR50s range).
